[1/3] Terrain material detail: material id in the colour alpha, shader grain for sand/grass/forest/road/rock/snow, flower flecks, wet and snow response. [2/3] Graphical minimap built from the height/colour bundle with water, roads, entity dots and a gold player marker; suppress the ASCII map in the GPU HUD. [3/3] Tests, README/ADR-032 and full gates.

impact_assessment.why: The GPU ground read as one flat texture and the ASCII minimap clashed with the 3D view; materials and a real map are the remaining visible quality gap.
impact_assessment.benefits: Distinct ground materials, weather response and a useful overhead map, all from data already sent to the browser.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the colour texture alpha now carries a material id; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; performance: one offscreen canvas and a little extra fragment math; visual: grain and wet/snow response could look noisy or wash out the palette.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the alpha consumer inside the GPU terrain shader, build the minimap once per world bundle, cap detail amplitudes, and verify day/night/rain captures before the gate.

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Phase 4 green: 190 tests (72.5s), hygiene, guidelines/map and secrets pass 4/4. GPU surface shipped: terrain material ids in the colour alpha drive sand ripple, grass/forest grain, flower flecks, road stones, rock strata and snow cover; wet rain darkens the ground and snow whitens it. The GPU HUD draws an offscreen terrain minimap with water, roads, entity dots and a gold player marker, and suppresses the ASCII map. Tests pin the material alpha, scene fields, show_map toggle and minimap hooks. Live Edge captures verified day, daylight rain, daylight snow, night rain and night snow. README and ADR-032 updated. checklists: passed; PRINCIPLE-018 commit/push skipped because the user did not authorize a commit.
Task 'aldervale-gpu-surface-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Weather-aware models: rain darkens figures and roofs with a wet sheen; snow caps up-facing surfaces, excluding fire and torch flames. [2/3] Water shading: fresnel sky reflection, sun glint, and rain ripple rings. [3/3] Flickering fire/torch/window point lights, tests, README/ADR-033 and full gates.

impact_assessment.why: Snow now covers the ground but not the buildings or characters, wet models look dry, water is a flat plane and firelight is static; these are the remaining visible weather mismatches.
impact_assessment.benefits: Snow and rain read consistently across terrain and models, lakes gain depth and sun glints, and fires feel alive without changing the simulation.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: lights gain an 'f' field; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; performance: a few extra fragment operations and per-light sin calls; visual: snow caps or wet specular can over-brighten models, and water glints can blow out.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use up-facing normals with a smoothstep, dim snow by daylight, exclude flame models from caps, keep wet specular low, bound flicker arrays at six, and verify day/night rain and snow captures.

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Phase 4 green: 190 tests (77.2s), hygiene, guidelines/map and secrets pass 4/4. Weather-response pass shipped: rain darkens models and adds a wet sheen, snow caps up-facing roofs/shoulders with flames excluded, water adds fresnel horizon reflection, a sun glint and rain ripple rings, and scene lights carry a flicker weight applied from a per-frame CPU array. Live Edge captures verified daylight snow caps, daylight and night rain darkening, and lake water with shoreline foam and rain ripples; the wet darkening was eased from 0.80 to 0.88 so the player stays readable at night. README and ADR-033 updated. checklists: passed; PRINCIPLE-018 commit/push skipped because the user did not authorize a commit.
Task 'aldervale-gpu-weather-response-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Weather-graded atmosphere: rain/snow shift the sky, horizon, fog colour and distance, dim the sun and flatten direct light. [2/3] Drifting cloud shadows over terrain and models; depth-graded turquoise shallows in the water. [3/3] Tests, README/ADR-034 and full gates.

impact_assessment.why: Snow and rain still happen under a bright blue sky and hard sun, and lakes read as one flat blue; the atmosphere does not yet match the weather.
impact_assessment.benefits: Overcast weather looks coherent, cloud shadows add motion to the ground, and water gains readable depth at the shoreline.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; performance: extra weather maths, fog uniforms and a cloud-shadow term per fragment; visual: overcast grading can crush contrast or make night scenes too bright.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Scale weather target colours by daylight, keep fog and cloud-shadow amounts bounded, centralise the palette in one JS helper, and verify day/night clear, rain, snow and lake captures.

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Phase 4 green: 190 tests (81.9s), hygiene, guidelines/map and secrets pass 4/4. Atmosphere pass shipped: weatherEnv() grades zenith/horizon/fog, shortens fog, dims the sun, flattens direct light, hides stars/moon and raises cloud cover for rain/snow; terrain and models share a drifting cloud-shadow term; water mixes turquoise shallows by smooth bilinear height depth into deep blue, raises opacity and uses weather fog. Live Edge captures verified clear day, overcast snow day, overcast rain day, night rain without stars, and a lake with smooth turquoise shallows and a sun glint; the first lake capture exposed blocky seabed patches, fixed with bilinear depth and stronger water opacity. README and ADR-034 updated. checklists: passed; PRINCIPLE-018 commit/push skipped because the user did not authorize a commit.
Task 'aldervale-gpu-overcast-v1' completed successfully.

[1/2] Layered sky clouds: two drifting fbm layers plus wisps, sun-lit cloud edges and wider sun/moon halos; clear weather gets more visible clouds. [2/2] Rain lightning flash overlay, tests, README/ADR-035 and full gates.

impact_assessment.why: The clear sky still reads as a mostly empty blue gradient, and rain has no lightning; clouds and storm flashes are the remaining atmosphere gaps.
impact_assessment.benefits: A richer sky in clear and overcast weather, better sun/moon presence, and occasional lightning that makes rain feel like a storm.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; performance: two extra fbm evaluations in the sky shader; visual: denser clouds can gray out clear days or wash out the horizon, and flashes can overexpose a frame.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep cloud coverage and sun-lit tint bounded, preserve the existing gradient and weather palette, make lightning rare and short, and verify clear/rain/snow captures.

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Phase 4 green: 190 tests (101.8s), hygiene, guidelines/map and secrets pass 4/4. Sky pass shipped: layered drifting fbm clouds with a high wisp layer, weather cloud bias (scattered clear / overcast rain-snow), sun-lit cloud tint, detail and horizon shading, wider sun/moon halos, and a rare double-pulse rain lightning overlay via lightningAt() and uFlash. Cloud frequency and opacity were tuned twice from captures to avoid vertical bands and oversized flat blobs. Live Edge captures verified clear day puffs, overcast rain and snow skies, and a night clear sky with stars and a moon halo; lightning is wired and compiled but the still captures did not catch a flash. README and ADR-035 updated. checklists: passed; PRINCIPLE-018 commit/push skipped because the user did not authorize a commit.
Task 'aldervale-gpu-sky-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Structured HUD status in the scene JSON: name, level, gold, HP, stamina, XP, potions, weapon/armor and quest. [2/3] Graphical status panel in the GPU client; suppress the ASCII bottom status rows while keeping messages, location plate and minimap; simplify the page header. [3/3] Tests, README/ADR-036 and full gates.

impact_assessment.why: The 3D scene is polished but its main status block is still five rows of ASCII text, which reads as a terminal overlay rather than a game HUD.
impact_assessment.benefits: Readable bars and gear/quest text, a cleaner view, and the same simulation data driving both the terminal and GPU HUDs.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the scene JSON gains a status object; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; performance: a few text/rect draws per frame; visual: the panel must fit the existing bottom scrim, not hide messages, and fall back to ASCII on small stages.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Only draw the panel when the server marks the status visible and the stage is at least 12.5px per row; skip exactly the five status rows; keep messages above the panel; test payload fields and live captures.

[1/2] Add a failing-first compact-layout test and fix the GPU status panel so the gear line clears the HP/STA/XP bars at 11-13px rows; verify in the live /play3d page at a mid-size stage. [2/2] Run the full project gate and commit.

impact_assessment.why: At 11-13px rows the compact GPU HUD draws the gear line through the HP/STA/XP bars; the full >=80px layout was verified but the compact branch was not.
impact_assessment.benefits: A readable HUD at common laptop window sizes without leaving the 5.2-row scrim or falling back to ASCII.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, drawing-only; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; visual: title, bars, gear and quest must stay inside the 5.2-row panel and clear each other down to the 11px threshold; test: page-string assertions only, so the live capture remains the visual proof.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Derive compact row positions from the panel height, clamp the gear baseline above the bar bottom, pin the geometry in a unit test, and verify at a compact stage plus the existing full stage.
